Definition
[Boundedly compact space and tangent cone] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0418 ↗ def:chow-iii-g14-pointed-gh 1. appG:G.20\group Metric cones

A metric space is boundedly compact if every closed bounded subset is compact. When the limit exists independently of $\alpha _i\to \infty $, its tangent cone at $p$ is \[ (T_pX,d_p,0_p)=\lim _{\alpha _i\to \infty }(X,\alpha _i d,p). \] For a Riemannian manifold this cone is $T_p\mathcal M\cong \mathbf E^n$.
